beats.sentence: The fire began in Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane.

semantic.subject: the fire
semantic.relationship: one small bakery as the origin of a city-wide fire
semantic.environment: Pudding Lane, a narrow street of timber houses

beats.visual_question: how do you show that something enormous started in one small, specific place?

mechanism.construction: Start on the doorway of the bakery in a period engraving of Pudding Lane, then pull out across the engraved street until the lane is one thin line in a 1666 map of the walled city.
mechanism.why: the origin only matters once you see how small it is against the city it destroyed

camera.from: extreme close on the bakery doorway in the engraving
camera.to: the whole walled city on the map, the lane a thin line
camera.motivation: context-reveal: begin on the origin, widen until its smallness against the city is the point

materials.must_show: an engraving of Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane
search: Pudding Lane bakery engraving Thomas Farriner
Great Fire of London Pudding Lane print

materials.must_show: a 1666 map of the City of London showing Pudding Lane
materials.why: the space the origin sits in
search: 1666 map City of London Pudding Lane

shots.action: the bakery engraving shrinks into its place on the map as the frame widens across the City of London

text.placement: beside the lane on the map

beats.mute_test: a whole city's story began at one small doorway

beats.sentence: In four days it destroyed 13,200 houses and 87 churches.
beats.visual_question: how do you make 13,200 lost houses feel like space rather than a number?

mechanism.construction: On the 1666 survey map, burned blocks are struck through street by street over four days until the destroyed area covers most of the walled city; the counts for houses and churches are the data the strike-through follows.
mechanism.why: the loss accumulates as area, so the scale arrives as space taken away

camera.from: the east end of the survey map
camera.to: the west edge where the burned area stops
camera.motivation: follows the burned area as it accumulates westward across the map

materials.must_show: a 1666 survey map of the burned area of the City of London
materials.why: the real extent of the loss
search: 1666 map burnt area London Leake survey

materials.must_show: the sourced counts of houses and churches destroyed
search: Great Fire of London houses destroyed 13,200

shots.action: burned blocks on the survey map are struck through block by block as the houses count reaches 13,200

beats.mute_test: most of the city on the map has been taken away

beats.sentence: The flames moved west on a strong east wind.

semantic.subject: the flames
semantic.environment: a strong east wind over the city

beats.visual_question: how do you show a wind pushing a fire across a city?

mechanism.construction: A painting of the fire seen from the river, tracked right-to-left so the smoke column leans and the burning skyline moves west with the camera.
mechanism.why: the direction of the camera matches the direction the wind pushes the flames

camera.from: the burning skyline at the east end of the painting
camera.to: the smoke leaning west over the unburned roofs
camera.motivation: flow: the camera travels with the wind, the way the fire did

materials.must_show: a contemporary painting of the Great Fire of London seen from the Thames
materials.why: shows the smoke and skyline the wind moved
search: Great Fire of London painting Thames 1666

shots.action: the painting slides past as the smoke in the painting leans west over the roofs

beats.mute_test: the fire is being pushed in one direction across the city

beats.sentence: Samuel Pepys buried his cheese in his garden.

semantic.subject: Samuel Pepys
semantic.relationship: a man protecting a small possession from the fire
semantic.change: cheese moved from house to ground

beats.visual_question: how do you show a person choosing what to save?

mechanism.construction: A portrait of Samuel Pepys, then a match-cut to his diary page for the day, the line about burying his Parmesan held in an inset detail.
mechanism.why: the possession passes from the man into the ground, recorded in his own hand

camera.from: Samuel Pepys's portrait, head and shoulders
camera.motivation: pushes in to the person making the choice before showing what he chose

materials.must_show: the portrait of Samuel Pepys by John Hayls

shots.action: the portrait of Pepys fills the frame as the camera closes on his face

camera.from: the top of the diary page
camera.motivation: the pan reads down the page to the record of what he buried

materials.must_show: Samuel Pepys's diary page for September 1666 mentioning the Parmesan cheese
materials.why: his own record of the act

shots.action: the diary page slides up until the cheese line sits in the inset

beats.mute_test: a man recorded hiding something precious from the fire

beats.visual_question: how do you hold a turn in the story without inventing a new picture?

mechanism.construction: The diary page from the previous shot stays in frame, darkened under the words, while the narration turns to what comes next.
mechanism.why: a turn in the story with no new fact; the words carry it over an image already established

camera.motivation: the stillness is the pause before the story turns; nothing new is shown yet

materials.must_show: Samuel Pepys's diary page for September 1666
materials.why: the established image the words sit on

shots.action: the diary page sinks back under the words as they land

beats.mute_test: a turn: there is more to this story
